title: Traffic Entropy Mitigation and Observation Protocol — WIP
content:
Purpose:
This doc describes a lightweight protocol (work-in-progress) for detecting, mitigating, and communicating high-entropy traffic patterns during cross-functional LLM rollouts and A/B experiments. The specific focus is on symptoms that indicate traffic distribution or user-behavior entropy is diverging from expected slices (e.g., a small set of inputs suddenly dominating, long-tail prompts spiking, bot/fuzz traffic, or cascading fallback amplification).

Context / motivation:
- We frequently run canaries and cohorted experiments that assume a relatively stable distribution of request types. LLMs amplify distribution shifts: a sudden change in a small but high-throughput cohort can distort quality telemetry and cost.
- Production incidents in the last 6 months with unexpected traffic concentration caused: token-cost overrun, high latency due to overheating a single model variant, and bad-signal contamination in evals.

Goals:
1) Detect entropy events rapidly with minimal manual overhead.
2) Provide deterministic mitigation steps (traffic shaping, temporary throttles, model variant pinning) so experiment owners can triage quickly.
3) Ensure cross-team visibility and a clear comms path for rollback or quarantine decisions.
4) Capture structured artifacts for postmortem and metric hygiene.

Scope / non-goals:
- In-scope: Hosted API experiments, Dedicated early-stage ramp, Console-driven A/B tests where telemetry hooks exist.
- Out-of-scope: fully air-gapped private deployments (those use a different incident path) and long-term cohort re-architecting (we will flag if structural changes are needed).

Definitions (working):
- Entropy event: An observable shift in request distribution within a rollout window such that at least one of the following holds:
  * Top-k request tokens or prompt templates account for > X% (configurable) of requests compared to baseline.
  * The rate of novel prompt shapes (new templates hashed by prompt-normalizer) exceeds threshold.
  * Sudden burst in short/long tail request lengths that breaks batching heuristics.
  * Elevation in downstream failure modes (rerank errors, hallucination reports) correlated with a subpopulation.
- Quarantine: temporary traffic isolation (slice-level) and/or automatic fallback to baseline model for affected cohort.

Metric signals (priority order):
1) Top-10 prompt-template share — daily and 5m; flag if top-1 share > 30% (configurable) or > baseline by 3x.
2) Token-per-request distribution shift (p50/p95/p99) compared to baseline windows.
3) Average generation latency and queue time by cohort/slice.
4) Cost per request (estimated GPU-token cost) spike correlated with request concentration.
5) Model quality regressions measured by key eval prompts or golden samples (if failing, immediate human review).
6) Synthetic probe failure rate (internal synthetic traffic that evaluates known behaviors).
7) Anomaly score from traffic-entropy detector (see algorithm notes).

Traffic-entropy detector (sketch):
- Input: time-bucketed bag-of-templates + token-length histogram per slice.
- Compute: normalized Shannon entropy on template distribution with exponential smoothing; compute KL divergence against baseline window; combine with token-length dispersion metric.
- Output: single entropy_score (0..1) and contributors list (top impacted templates).
- Notes: detector must be lightweight (run in streaming analytics) and include a tunable sensitivity param per experiment.

Alerting and severity tiers:
- Severity 3 (info): entropy_score > 0.25 for 3 buckets (5m) — notify experiment owner via console comment and Slack bot.
- Severity 2 (investigate): entropy_score > 0.5 or top-1 template > 25% relative share and correlated latency/cost increase — page on-call experiment steward, open ephemeral incident doc.
- Severity 1 (action): entropy_score > 0.75 OR detected synthetic-probe regressions OR quality alerts on golden set — trigger immediate mitigation policy (see below) and senior product + SRE comms.

Mitigation playbook (automated first, then human):
Automated (fast path):
1) Apply temporary rate cap to top offender template(s) at 30% of baseline rate for 10 minutes (configurable).
2) If latency > SLO and top offender also present, auto-route that cohort to baseline model variant.
3) Emit structured audit event to rollout console containing trigger conditions and actions taken.

Human (escalation):
1) Experiment steward validates audit event, inspects contributors list, and decides to either extend caps, fully quarantine slice, or roll model.
2) If quarantine: create a cohort-level traffic-split change (console) moving affected slice to fallback with ephemeral note and savepoint.
3) If rollback: follow standard rollback checklist (force traffic to previous model version, snapshot telemetry windows, notify CS/legal if customer-facing).

Communication protocol:
- Automated messages: Slack bot posts brief with entropy_score, top templates, immediate action.
- Owner comms: Experiment owner gets an in-console task with one-click acknowledge + triage link.
- Incident path: Severity 2/1 also triggers the rollout oncall and the product PM; Severity 1 summons an ad-hoc war-room.
- External comms: If customer cohorts impacted (dedicated customers), trigger CS playbook and legal notification as per existing incident policy.

Console and observability UX additions (product requests):
- Entropy panel per run: sparklines for entropy_score, top template heatmap, token-length histogram, and synthetic probe pass-rate.
- One-click mitigation buttons: apply-cap, quarantine-slice, reroute-to-baseline. All actions must produce immutable audit events.
- Historical replay: ability to replay the last N minutes of requests for forensic debugging (redact PII).

Open questions / design tradeoffs:
- Sensitivity vs noise: low thresholds produce many false positives for marketing bursts — need a suppression layer for known campaign traffic.
- Auto-mitigation aggressiveness: balance between preventing cost/regression and blocking legitimate viral usage.
- Template normalization: how aggressively to normalize prompts (we are currently hashing full prompt templates, but should we remove user variables?).
- Cross-region coordination: entropy may look local — how to correlate global view for Dedicated customers?

Quick checklists (for on-call or steward):
1) Acknowledge alert and open ephemeral incident doc.
2) Inspect contributors list and top templates.
3) Run synthetic probe set against baseline and candidate variant.
4) If auto-mitigation active, review audit event and extend or revert after 10m observation window.
5) If quarantine or rollback triggered, notify CS and schedule a postmortem.

Postmortem artifacts to capture (minimum):
- Time-series snapshot (5m buckets) of entropy_score, top-10 template share, latency, cost, quality evals.
- Audit log of mitigation actions and owner acknowledgements.
- Root cause hypothesis (bot/fuzz, campaign, model behavior, instrumentation bug).
- Action items (fix instrumentation, adjust sensitivity, long-term guardrails).

Implementation roadmap (next 3 sprints):
- Sprint 1: implement streaming entropy detector prototype in rollout analytics; add console alert stub and Slack bot integration.
- Sprint 2: build lightweight auto-mitigation primitives (rate cap and variant routing), immutable audit events.
- Sprint 3: UX polish (entropy panel), suppression rules for known campaigns, and controlled-wide experiments to tune thresholds.

Immediate next steps (owner = Evelyn):
- Set up meeting w/ analytics infra and SRE to scope detector ops (this week).
- Create JIRA epic for auto-mitigation primitives and link to this doc (JIRA-RINF-8421).
- Seed golden sample set for quick quality checks.

Notes to self / working assumptions:
- Keep mitigation actions reversible and conservative by default.
- Preserve auditability: every console action must be tied to a user and reason.
- We will iterate thresholds on a per-experiment basis — default sensibility is more important than per-case tuning initially.

Appendix: short example scenario
- Day 0: New reranker canary enabled for 5% traffic slice. Baseline top-10 prompt share stable.
- Day 1 (09:23): entropy detector raises severity-2 — template T-57 jumps to 28% of canary traffic and p99 latency grows 1.8x.
- Automated action: T-57 rate capped to 30% of previous rate and affected requests routed to baseline model variant. Audit event posted.
- Steward: confirms automated mitigation, schedules quarantine for further analysis, closes incident after 40m when metrics stabilize.

If you're reading this and want to help: add comments below, add cases (past incidents) and tag me (@evelyn) on Slack.
